summary.headline: GSFC Q2 FY27 consolidated sales rose 49% YoY, but PBT fell 42% and PAT fell 38% as fertilizer EBIT collapsed to INR17 crores on raw material costs.
summary.overview: Revenue hit a record Q2 on DAP realisation support, but sulfur (up 327%) and natural gas (up 62%) costs crushed fertilizer margins. Fertilizer EBIT fell to INR17 crores from INR224 crores a year earlier, while Industrial Products EBIT rose to INR66 crores from INR54 crores on better caprolactam, nylon and Anone realisations. Management said the company has no long-term debt, and it has approved a roughly INR3,000 crore phosphoric and sulfuric acid project at Sikka. H2 outlook hinges on the NBS subsidy rates for October to March, which have not yet been notified.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: Sales up 55% YoY (+INR1,387 crores) despite volume down 6% to 5.69 lakh MT from 6.08 lakh MT. DAP revenue rose INR1,659 crores on the government DAP special package, but EBIT fell to INR17 crores from INR224 crores.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Sales up INR185 crores (30% YoY). Caprolactam sales up INR58 crores and nylon up INR60 crores on higher realisations; Anone up INR36 crores on volume; TGU up INR26 crores; melamine down INR5 crores. Caprolactam-benzene spread rose to USD 849/MT from USD 512/MT.

guidance_outlook: Management was optimistic on H2 FY27, conditional on the NBS subsidy rates for 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027, which had not been notified at the time of the call.
Management said the Q2 profit deficit would be compensated in the next quarter if the subsidy rates are raised and approved.
Caprolactam-benzene spread is expected to moderate in Q3 FY27 as regional supply normalises.
Melamine and technical-grade urea demand expected steady; HX crystal exports may improve given subdued domestic demand.
Solar power arrangement at Sikka expected to save INR20-25 crores per quarter.
Management said no buyback or other value-creation measures have been discussed by the Board yet.
capex_capacity: Phosphoric acid and sulfuric acid (PA-SA) project at Sikka: about INR3,000 crores, EPC contract recently awarded, 30-33 months to completion. It is expected to meet 50% of DAP and NPK raw material needs captively.
C-Train modification for 1,200 MT per day APS production in place of DAP at Sikka commissioned on 23 October 2026, per market requirement.
Management estimated about 20% margin from producing phosphoric acid in-house versus purchasing it.
Rock procurement will be under a long-term contract, but contractors will not fix prices, so the price will be set at the purchase date.
demand_pricing: Rabi season opens with fertilizer inventory at the highest level in 3 years, especially urea and NPK, which intensifies competition.
Subdued southwest monsoon and low reservoir levels in southern India likely to constrain fertilizer demand.
DAP-NPK price distortion is steering farmers toward DAP, hurting NPK offtake. NBS rates are seen as key to resolving this.
Management said DAP margin is about 4% (fully compensated under the advantage/disadvantage regime) and urea margin about 3-4%. NPK margins depend on the subsidy rates still to come.

Urea subsidy receipts were received up to the third week of October. Management said urea's share of the INR3,400 crore subsidy receivable is only about INR100-300 crores, which the company expects to recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and economics of the Sikka capex for phosphoric and sulfuric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Project financed at about INR3,000 crores, EPC awarded, 30-33 months to complete. About 50% of DAP and NPK requirement to be captively sourced, with about 20% margin from in-house PA production.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook given volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was optimistic, citing the pending NBS subsidy rates from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. It said the Q2 deficit would be made up in Q3 if rates rise, and that cost cuts under a BCG-suggested plan are being applied at Sikka.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR3,400 crore subsidy receivable relates to urea?
qa_highlights.answer: Urea subsidy was received up to the third week of October. Urea accounts for only about INR100-200 crores (up to INR300 crores), with the bulk tied to DAP and NPK.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any value-creation plan such as a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback or other measures have been discussed at the Board yet; management will revert at an appropriate time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operational efficiency gain beyond subsidy?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar power at Sikka replacing costly grid power is expected to add about INR20-25 crores per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How is distribution and Industrial Products growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Fertilizer distribution is set by the government. Industrial products are sold on market demand pan-India, and management sees better IP prospects from captive raw materials and product mix, since chemical prices are not under MRP control.

risks_watch: NBS subsidy rates for Oct 2026 to Mar 2027 are not yet notified. Fertilizer margins depend almost entirely on them.
Urea subsidy pool gas rate finalisation between FICC and GAIL has been pending since April 2026, so urea subsidy may still be revised.
Sulfur (+327%) and natural gas (+62%) costs remain elevated; Middle East and Europe tensions are a key swing factor.
Record fertilizer inventory ahead of Rabi, weak monsoon and southern reservoir levels, and DAP-NPK price distortion may pressure volumes and NPK offtake.
Caprolactam-benzene spread expected to moderate in Q3 FY27, which would weigh on the caprolactam-nylon chain.
Sikka PA-SA project runs 30-33 months, and its ultimate margin depends on PA and sulfur prices at commissioning.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and the balance sheet, but guarded on margins: management repeatedly deferred H2 profitability to the unannounced NBS subsidy rates. Answers on buybacks and value creation were non-committal.
key_quotes: So the company has delivered its ever highest Q2 and H1 top lines, achieving total sales of INR4,711 crores on a stand-alone basis in quarter 2 '26-'27
The subsidy is very important because whatever margins are coming, it is from subsidy.
Whatever the deficit in the profits we have incurred during the last quarter, this will be compensated in the next quarter.
